messages:
maria: FYI incoming ticket from BigQueryCorp — their nightly embeddings pipeline started getting intermittent 429s around 02:00 UTC last night.
maria: stack: python SDK running in k8s cronjob, uses 10 parallel workers, each building large batches client-side.
kevin: can you paste a sanitized sample of the failing response and their request pattern?
maria: pasted redacted log snippet in the ticket:

support-bot: ```json
{"request_id":"r-xyz-987","model":"embed-large-1536","batch_size":1024,"workers":10,"error":{"status":429,"message":"Rate limit exceeded","retry_after":3}}
```

alex: 10 workers * 1024 per request = very spiky. Even if avg throughput fits, bursts blow past per-second burst caps.
julia: they also reported earlier a dimension mismatch that returned vectors length 1280 while their pipeline expected 1536 — they said they retried individual items after that error.
kevin: dimension mismatch + per-item retry = classic amplification. Also check if their retry ignores `Retry-After` header.
maria: logs show `Retry-After: 3` in responses. they currently do simple immediate retries up to 5 times.

sre-oncall: checked account limits: host-level burst limit ~200 reqs/s and token burst ~10k tokens/s. the customer's pattern exceeds per-second request bursts when all workers fire.

kevin: short-term fixes we should recommend to customer (support playbook):
- drop concurrency from 10 -> 2-4 while job runs
- reduce batch_size from 1024 -> 128-256
- add exponential backoff with jitter and respect `Retry-After` header
- avoid retrying individual items on schema/dimension failures; fail the batch and inspect

maria: sending a tiny backoff example for python SDK:

support-bot: ```python
import time, random

def backoff(attempt):
    base = 0.5
    return base * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 0.2)

for attempt in range(6):
    resp = client.embeddings.create(...)
    if resp.status_code == 429:
        wait = int(resp.headers.get('Retry-After', backoff(attempt)))
        time.sleep(wait)
    else:
        break
```

alex: include a curl repro for them to validate after changes:

support-bot: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-1536","input":["a","b","c"],"batch_size":256}'
```

kevin: internal repro steps for SRE/perf team to confirm throttling:
1) launch N concurrent clients (10-12) sending POST /v1/embeddings with batch_size=1024
2) capture response headers `x-rate-limit-limit`, `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset` and `Retry-After`
3) simulate dimension-mismatch downstream and a naive per-item retry loop to observe amplification

sre-oncall: I'll run a k6 scenario in a maintenance window and capture the headers. saw sample repro run return `x-rate-limit-limit: 200`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 167` during spike.

julia: customer-facing FAQ lines to include:
Q: Why did this happen suddenly? A: Likely their job became more parallel (cron change) or model/batching changed, plus we tightened burst safety recently on 03/10 which makes high instantaneous bursts surface as 429s.
Q: "Retry-After" sometimes 0 — what does that mean? A: It can mean the next token window is immediate; still, clients must add backoff/jitter to avoid tight retry loops.

maria: draft reply to customer (please review):

support-bot: "Thanks — we see high parallel bursts plus some retry amplification from a dimension mismatch. Short-term: reduce concurrency & batch size and add exponential backoff that respects `Retry-After`. We'll run an internal repro and can offer a quota bump or Dedicated capacity if you need sustained high throughput. Can you also confirm SDK version and whether you changed model/batching recently?"

alex: link to docs to include: https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/best-practices#batching-and-rate-limits and https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/model-dimensions

kevin: follow-ups assigned: @kevin will upload k6 script and headers capture; @sre-oncall to run repro and paste logs; @alex to own customer comms and quota discussion.

maria: closure checklist for support:
- [ ] customer reduced concurrency/backoff applied and confirms 429s reduced
- [ ] internal repro run and headers captured
- [ ] CS evaluated quota/dedicated options and proposed next steps

sre-oncall: posting quick smoke logs when done. initial run shows burst throttle consistent with the customer's pattern — will post detailed captures.

maria: thanks everyone — will update ticket once we have repro artifacts and customer ack.
